clue.text: Labour leader overwhelmed by swing voter's disgust

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is swamped and surrounded by it, so the leader's letter goes inside the shuffled word
to swing is to sway about, so the letters of voter are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word voter supplies its five letters; the 's is the surface's possessive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: L is the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A floating voter is sickened by the Labour Party's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swing' rearranges VOTER to REVOT, and 'overwhelmed by' puts L, the leader of Labour, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolt as a noun is a feeling of revulsion, a synonym of disgust.

clue.text: Keep in mind Lear's regularly ignored servant

parts.note: to retain a fact is to keep it in mind

indicators.note: every other letter is skipped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: taking the second and fourth letters of Lear's gives E and R

explanation.surface: Remember that King Lear's servant is often overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a household servant, especially one who has served a family a long time.

clue.text: Realist rambling in the middle of Provence is adaptable

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the middle pair
the middle of an eight-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of Provence are V and E

indicators.note: rambling is wandering aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth person roaming the heart of Provence copes with anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' an eight-letter word is its central pair, so the shuffled realist sits between two letters of Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile has many skills and can turn to different tasks, so is flexible.

clue.text: Put in position face up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Something is placed with its front upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face up' reads like lying the right way round; it is DIAL reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid, the past of lay, means placed or set down, as a table is laid.

clue.text: Agreement to kill Bond

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is the underworld deal to murder someone, as in 'put a ... out on him'
second meaning: a bond is a binding agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Bond tempts you towards the spy, which fits the killing, but here it is the legal sense of a binding deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is hired under a contract, and a bond is a formal written undertaking, another name for a contract.

clue.text: Single start not entirely involving a great deal of effort

definitions.text: involving a great deal of effort

parts.note: one means single

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to rouse is to start or startle, as game is roused from cover

explanation.surface: Starting alone and only part-way makes a task hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and demanding, requiring much exertion.

clue.text: Conservative maintaining model fled earlier vanishing quickly

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the Conservative holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: earlier puts the fled word before the model word

parts.note: ran means fled
to sit is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A Tory supporting a model who ran off disappears fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is a verb here: to sit for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory lasts only a short while before passing away, so it is fleeting.

clue.text: Crime of American frontiersman initially dismissed

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter, and dismissed says it is sent away

parts.note: Kit Carson was a famous American frontiersman of the Old West

explanation.surface: An American pioneer's offence was initially thrown out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Fictional wizard with time for power of rock

indicators.note: time for power means T stands in place of P

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's novels
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A storybook wizard uses time in place of the power of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' reads like music, but it is the verb meaning to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to sway unsteadily back and forth, so it is a synonym of rock as a verb.

clue.text: Georgia has learning in abundance

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
lore is learning or traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: The state of Georgia has plenty of scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore comes after a noun to mean in great numbers, plentiful.

clue.text: Conclude with former head of state having time in art gallery

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the late Queen, a former head of state
MIN, short for minute, is a measure of time

explanation.surface: A former president wraps up a visit by spending time in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II; the Tate is a London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, so it is a synonym of conclude.

clue.text: American novel's heroine brought about something advantageous

indicators.note: brought about is a nautical turn, a ship coming round to face the other way, so the heroine's name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: The heroine of an American novel caused something useful to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' looks like 'caused', but it is the sailing term for turning a ship round. The novel is Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that gives you a benefit or advantage.

clue.text: By no means all acclaim amuses prayer leader

indicators.note: By no means all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone who receives praise is entertained by a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam is the person who leads the congregation in prayer at a mosque.

clue.text: Macron's refusal to admit working on moral discernment is straightforward

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the refusal takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: Macron is the French president, and non is French for no
ON means working, as a switched-on machine is
a moral sense is the ability to discern right from wrong

explanation.surface: The French president refuses to accept that judging right and wrong is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-nonsense approach is plain and direct, without frills or fuss: a synonym of straightforward.

clue.text: Jovial king finding terrible ogre a fear inducing sight

parts.note: jolly means jovial
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful monarch meets a dreadful ogre and is frightened by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ogre and king suggest a fairy tale; the sight is the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones pirate flag was flown to terrify the crew of a ship about to be attacked.

clue.text: Defoe's last good book's a typical example

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: E is the final letter of Defoe
PI, short for pious, means good
a tome is a book, often a large one

explanation.surface: The final good book by Daniel Defoe is representative of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitome of something is a perfect instance that embodies its essential qualities.

clue.text: Arrange it for the most part with a solicitor

indicators.note: only the greater part of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, or sex appeal
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: Arrange it, mostly, with a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but a tout is someone who solicits buyers, such as a ticket tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out things is to lay them out in order, so the phrase is a synonym of arrange.

clue.text: Secret known by worker

parts.note: under means known by, as in travelling under a false name
a hand is a worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A labourer is known to be keeping something hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: To operate under a name is to be known by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealings are done secretly and deceitfully, out of sight.

clue.text: Fellow finding note after return of oddly rejected dairy produce

indicators.note: after places the note behind the reversed letters

parts.note: Gene is a man's name, a fellow

indicators.note: return means the letters come back the other way, read backwards
the odd-numbered letters are thrown out, leaving the even ones

parts.note: dropping the first, third and fifth letters of dairy leaves A and R
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man finds a note after his rejected dairy goods are returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a noun, the dairy goods, but it is the verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to bring something into being, so it is a synonym of the verb produce.

clue.text: Staggered by Republican employing a slippery customer

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the Republican holds the next piece within it

parts.note: red is the colour of the Republican Party in the US
an eel is slippery, and the phrase is used for a shifty person

explanation.surface: Someone was shocked when a Republican took on a shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour associated with the US Republican Party, as in red states.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeled means swayed or lurched unsteadily, so it shares a sense with staggered.

clue.text: Cross about pal almost becoming someone to walk all over

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the cross is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church rood screen

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: Someone angry with a friend nearly becomes a pushover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is ROOD, the church crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others treat them badly without resisting, a pushover.

clue.text: Shorten brigade training

indicators.note: training licks recruits into a new shape, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A military brigade's training course is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to condense it, making a shorter version.

clue.text: Nursed by David Lynch with great enthusiasm

indicators.note: nursed by means held in the arms of the following words, so the letters are carried inside them

parts.note: the letters run from inside David into Lynch

explanation.surface: Someone was cared for by the film director David Lynch with real passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something avidly is to do it eagerly and keenly.

clue.text: Fellow powerless to rent out house in the Alps

indicators.note: power is P, so powerless means without the letter P

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
to let is to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A broke man rents out a home in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house with overhanging roof, typical of Swiss Alpine villages.

clue.text: Right after, this revolutionary order of architecture becomes affected

indicators.note: after places R behind the reshuffled letters
revolutionary means turning everything over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture

explanation.surface: A revolutionary style of building after this becomes pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ionic order is the classical column style with scrolled capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is theatrical and overdone, so it is a synonym of affected in the sense of put on.

clue.text: Expertise shown in section on ice

parts.note: to ice someone is gangster slang for killing them

explanation.surface: Ability on display in a portion of an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' suggests skating, but it is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill is practised ability, a synonym of expertise.

clue.text: Not a slave released ultimately left

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one, and left means it is abandoned

parts.note: a released prisoner has been freed

explanation.surface: A freed slave eventually departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the past tense of leave; here it means the last letter of FREED is left off.
explanation.definitionFit: A free person is at liberty and owned by no one, the opposite of a slave.

clue.text: An advantage to move gradually

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ... is a slight advantage, as in having the ... over rivals
second meaning: to ... forward is to inch along slowly

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a small lead over competitors, and the verb means to creep along bit by bit.

clue.text: Why they say Heather embraces telling porkies

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within arms, so the plant takes the sounded letter inside it

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: they say means the word is to be heard, giving a letter sounding like it

parts.note: the word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a woman called Heather is telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Porkies is British rhyming slang: pork pies = lies. Heather is the plant, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling porkies means telling untruths, and lying is saying what is false.

clue.text: Extremely theatrical behaviour from Hindu god after tune's cut short

indicators.note: after means the god's name follows the shortened tune
to cut something short is to lop off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a melody is a tune
Rama is a Hindu god, an avatar of Vishnu

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity's overacting follows when a song is stopped early.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is exaggerated, sensational emotion, like the stagey plays the name comes from.

clue.text: Bear's stomach

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bear something is to put up with it
second meaning: to stomach is to endure, as in 'I can't stomach it'

explanation.walkthrough: Bear's looks like an animal's belly, but both words are verbs for putting up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to endure or accept something unpleasant without protest.

clue.text: One involved in plot against the French college official

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so A goes into the plot

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground
A means one, as in a single thing
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A conspirator against the French is a university officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy, but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a ceremonial officer at some universities and colleges, leading processions.
